events.text:
## Recommendation
- Boat fishing for salmon looks weak at all four ports. Start at St. Joseph, the only port with a recent boat chinook or coho report, and expect a few fish rather than a good bite.
- Troll 30 to 60 feet of water off St. Joseph, the depths where the latest boat reports caught fish.
- Use small crankbaits and chartreuse or green spoons.
- Check the wind before you go. Recent gusts reached 40+ mph, so use Muskegon or the river as a fallback if it's rough.

## Why
- St. Joseph had the best recent boat report, with boats catching a few coho and chinook on crankbaits and spoons (St. Joseph, 2023-04-26).
- South Haven's latest boat report was slow for salmon, so I'd skip it for now (South Haven, 2023-04-26).
- Grand Haven has no recent boat salmon report, and its April reports describe slow action and dirty river water, so I have little basis to recommend it (Grand Haven, 2023-04-20).
- Muskegon's latest boat report had a few chinook at 30 to 60 feet on green and chartreuse spoons, but an earlier boat report there was slow (Muskegon, 2023-04-26 and 2023-04-20).

## Evidence
**My ratings for this week (0 to 4, boat salmon):**
- St. Joseph: 1 (below average). Latest boat coho and chinook were quality 1 (St. Joseph, 2023-04-26).
- Muskegon: 1 (below average). Boat chinook were quality 1 at 30 to 60 feet (Muskegon, 2023-04-26). An earlier boat report was quality 0 for coho (Muskegon, 2023-04-20).
- South Haven: 0 (slow). Boat anglers targeting salmon had slow fishing (South Haven, 2023-04-26).
- Grand Haven: not rated. I'd expect 0 to 1 based on its slow April reports and dirty river water (Grand Haven, 2023-04-20).

**Recent reports (latest is 6 days old, 12 days for Grand Haven):**
- St. Joseph boats: coho spread from 10 to 60 feet, with some anglers deeper than 60 feet. Small crankbaits and spoons worked best (St. Joseph, 2023-04-26).
- Muskegon boats: "Boats trolling in 30 to 60 feet of water caught a few Chinook salmon." Chartreuse and green spoons worked well (Muskegon, 2023-04-26).
- South Haven: pier and boat salmon fishing both slow (South Haven, 2023-04-26).

**Past seasons (history, not current):**
- In early May of 2022, when the water was near 46 F, the best St. Joseph boat report was quality 3 for coho, with the best depth at 30 feet (St. Joseph, 2022-05-04). That was a single week, and that buoy read 50 F.
- Other similar early-May weeks were mostly quality 0 to 1 (South Haven, Grand Haven, Muskegon, 2022-05-04 and 2022-04-27).

**Conditions now:**
- Live conditions were unavailable. The tool returned a summary for the week before May 2, not today's readings or a forecast.
- That week's satellite surface water was 45 to 47 F at all four ports (Conditions summary, week before 2023-05-02). That is cooler than the 52 to 58 F range salmon prefer, according to NY DEC guidance.
- Upwelling winds blew 33 to 39 hours that week, with gusts to 43 to 47 mph (Conditions summary, week before 2023-05-02).

## Caveats
- The newest boat report is from April 26, so it's a week or more old and the season moves fast in spring.
- The forecast for this week and today's buoy readings were not available, so check the wind and water before you launch.
- Grand Haven's boat data is too old and thin to rate. Use the 0 to 1 range as my guess, not a finding.
- The 2022 St. Joseph result is one week of history and may not repeat.

## Sources
- DNR bulletin, Apr 26, 2023 (Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3573537
- DNR bulletin, Apr 20, 2023 (Grand Haven, Muskegon): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3561fa6
- DNR bulletin, Apr 12, 2023 (Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven, St. Joseph): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3548e2b
- DNR bulletin, May 4, 2022 (history, St. Joseph and others): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3166173
